newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Quiet trade drags noon Australia stocks off highs.
newsitem.headline: Quiet trade drags noon Australia stocks off highs.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2506 -2.0 US 30yr cl 6.88 -0.03
10yrbond futs 92.230 +0.110 Gold NY 339.65 Lon fix 339.80
NIKKEI closed, market holiday FTSE cl 4455.6 +10.6
*Stocks off morning peaks as little support found at higher levels. Vol 119.54 million, A$290.34 million value, 798 stocks traded, 295 steady, 300 up, 203 down.
A lack of buying pulled Australian stocks down from their morning highs on Monday and dampened any enthusiam for the market to break record highs after the strong rally on Wall Street, brokers said.
By 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 6.4 points higher at 2,498.0, off a morning high of 2,509.9.
June share price index futures were up two points down at 2,506, a 11 point premium to the underlying index.
"There has been a lack of buying this morning, so there was no support to keep the market at its earlier levels," said Peter Struk at brokers Reynolds and Co.
Brokers said there would be a mild negative effect on the Australian gold sector following reports that the reserves of the Busang gold desposit in Indonesia had been overstated.
"The effect is likely to be negative as it will make investors more sceptical the information given in future gold finds," one Sydney based broker said.

"The malaise in the gold sector, with the weaker gold price, is set to continue for some time with the Bre-X situtation," said Mark Pervan at brokers Daiwa Securities. The Australia gold index fell slightly after Bre-X said an independent report found the Busang estimates were based on falsified data.
Shares in Golden Valley, which has a disputed claim on part of the Busang project, fell over 13 percent to 45 cents after the Bre-X announcement.
Interest in John Fairfax waned a little by noon with the shares sligtly off their morning high.
Speculation rose that media baron Kerry Packer may make a long-rumoured bid for the newspaper group after he withdrew a deal to take management control of the Sydney Casino.
Sydney Casino remained weak, while Packer's media group PBL was the biggest faller among the blue-chips as the group would have to pay a top price for Fairfax, brokers said.
Stocks fell across the board, with mining, engineering, paper, telecommunications, gold and building materials stocks lower in particular.
In other market news, Australian bond yields were close to the day's lows ahead of the lunchtime recess, although a sharp jump in the ANZ job ads briefly knocked the rally off course.
By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.75 percent, down 11 basis points.
The Australian dollar shrugged off early selling at midday aided by a strong partial data on the labour market. At 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), the dollar was trading at US$0.7826/31.
